faq.q: Is a window AC cheaper than a split AC?
faq.a: Yes — window ACs are 30–40% cheaper than split ACs at the same tonnage. A 1-ton window AC under ₹25,000 does the same cooling as a 1-ton split AC that costs ₹35,000–₹40,000. The trade-off is higher noise (52–60 dB vs 38–45 dB for split) and they take up window space.

faq.q: What size room does a 1-ton window AC cool?
faq.a: A 1-ton window AC is ideal for rooms between 100–150 sq ft. For a 150–200 sq ft room, go 1.5-ton. Below 100 sq ft, 0.75-ton or 1-ton still works — you'll just run it cooler or shorter cycles.

faq.q: Do window ACs need a stabilizer?
faq.a: Most window ACs under ₹25,000 in 2026 come with built-in stabilizers that handle 150V–290V. If your area has frequent voltage swings or drops below 150V, buy a separate 4 kVA stabilizer. Brands like Voltas and Lloyd include stabilizer-free operation in their marketing.

faq.q: How much electricity does a 1-ton window AC use?
faq.a: A 1-ton inverter window AC uses about 0.7–1.0 units per hour in normal mode. Running 8 hours a day for 30 days = 170–240 units/month, which is roughly ₹1,700–₹2,400 on most Indian residential tariff plans. Non-inverter models use 15–25% more.

faq.q: Can I install a window AC myself?
faq.a: Technically yes — most come with a fitting kit and foam strips. But the gas-charging ports need a technician to check for leaks. Most Indian brands offer free installation with the unit, or charge ₹500–₹1,500 for wall-mounting brackets. Budget ₹1,000–₹2,000 for installation if not included.
